correctness.rationale: The unique a^n factor defines exactly one run of length n for each symbol a. Deleting a there destroys that factor, whereas deleting a in another run preserves it and cannot join two a-runs. Root both latter outputs at the preserved factor: equality of the resulting linear strings forces all source letters between the deleted indices to agree. Different deleted symbols are distinguished by letter counts. Thus the mass of each descendant is its source run length divided by q^n. For lengths at most n−2, count bounded runs via the q^(n−ℓ−2) extensions of each factor b a^ℓ c with b,c ≠ a. For ℓ=n−1 there are q occurrences of a^(n−1), exactly two in the length-n run. This covers n=2 and the zero multiplicity for binary runs of length n−1. The total number also agrees with the count of unequal consecutive letters, (q−1)q^(n−1). The supplied verifier and log were inspected, not executed; their finite results are corroboration only.
